Subject: Sales discovery: model-fit, quantization trade study & next steps

Hi Tara / Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our discovery: we heard that FinLedger needs an LLM for:
- high-precision customer support categorization and routing (short prompts, strict correctness)
- long form policy summarization (long-context, retrieval + generation)
- reranking for candidate answers in the triage flow

Model fit & initial recommendations
- Candidate models to evaluate: Llama-3-70B (instruction-tuned), Mistral-Instruct-16B (cost-friendly), and Redmond-2-34B (Redwood-curated—higher-quality for longer context).
- Baseline evals we recommend: correctness on labeled testset, instruction-following score (human or synthetic), latency/throughput under 200ms p50 SLA, and hallucination audit on retrieval prompts.

Quantization / throughput tuning — high level
- AWQ (4-bit) gives the strongest throughput win on GPU for many transformer blocks but can introduce degradation on long-tail instruction-following prompts.
- GPTQ often preserves quality better than aggressive AWQ variants but has slower encode/decode in some runtimes.
- FP8 provides the best fidelity (closest to FP16/FP32) with modest runtime gains — good when quality is critical.

Attachments & links I shared (attached to this thread):
- redwood-benchmarks-q2-2026.xlsx (latency/throughput by model + quantization profile)
- finledger-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (recommended prompt set + labels)
- trade study (link): https://redwood.ai/trade-studies/quantization-awq-gptq-fp8

Proposed next steps
1) We (Redwood) provide temporary eval access to your team for the sandbox and upload the prompt set (we've attached v1).
2) Rishi to run a targeted internal bench on your longest-context prompts and produce a short trade study with recommended quantization per model.
3) Schedule a 45-minute technical follow-up next week to review results and discuss pricing/throughput options.

Can you confirm: 1) the three prompt groups (support categorization / policy summary / reranking) are the right priorities, and 2) who on your side should get eval access?

Thanks —

Hi Tara / Marissa —

Thanks — I ran a focused internal bench on the three priority prompt groups using your prompt-set v1. Short summary and recommended configs below. Full bench (raw numbers + waveform traces) is in the linked sheet.

Summary (high level)
- AWQ (4-bit, Redwood runtime tuned): throughput improvements ~1.8x–2.2x vs FP16 depending on batch/seq distribution. Latency p50 improves substantially; p95 improvement depends on batching.
- GPTQ variants: quality on instruction-following is typically better than aggressive AWQ for Llama-family models, but encoding latency is ~10–15% higher than AWQ in our runtime.
- FP8: quality is closest to FP16 across all models, with 1.1x–1.3x throughput improvement vs FP16 — good middle ground if you need near-native quality.

Quality regressions (what we saw)
- For short, instruction-following prompts (support categorization): AWQ-4 produced measurable drops on two out of five long-tail label classes for Llama-3-70B (precision drop of ~3–5% on those labels). GPTQ preserved those classes better; FP8 preserved almost all classes within <1% difference vs FP16.
- For long-context summarization: AWQ artifacts showed up as occasional tokenization/continuation inconsistencies on prompts >2k tokens for Redmond-2-34B; we recommend FP8 or hybrid (FP8 for encoder/attention-critical layers, AWQ for MLP-heavy layers) for long-context workloads.

Recommended configurations per workload
- Support categorization (short prompts, high correctness): Mistral-Instruct-16B @ GPTQ or FP8 (prefer FP8 if budget allows).
- Policy summarization (long context): Redmond-2-34B @ FP8 or hybrid FP8/AWQ.
- Reranking (throughput-sensitive): Llama-3-70B @ AWQ-4 with a small downstream reranker ensemble to catch edge cases.

Cost/throughput delta (rough)
- AWQ-4: ~40–55% lower per-token GPU cost vs FP16 (depending on packing/batch).
- GPTQ: ~25–40% lower cost vs FP16, higher CPU overhead at load time for some variants.
- FP8: ~10–25% lower cost vs FP16 but best quality preservation.

Deliverables & timeline
- I can publish the full bench and recommended per-model profiles by EOD Monday (June 29) and grant sandbox access to your two people now.
- If you want, we can run a short 24-hour A/B eval (FP16 vs FP8 vs AWQ) on a 5k-prompt sample and return a small quality delta report within 48 hours.

Links: trade-study & raw bench: https://drive.google.com/open?id=benchmark-sheet-2026

Let me know if you'd like a short notes call to go through the per-prompt failure modes — happy to walk through examples.

Cheers,
Rishi
Staff Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
